newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan rice rates seen down as new crop arrives.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan rice rates seen down as new crop arrives.

text.p: Pakistani rice prices may tumble next week as IRRI-6 rice has reached the market in southern parts of Sindh province, dealers said on Thursday.
Basmati rice will reach the market early next month, exporter Khalid Ghori said.
"We have started purchases of IRRI-6 rice from the 1996/97 (July-June) crop from Thatta District in southern Sindh," Khalid Ghori of Matco Rice Processing said. "The rice crop is good."
He said the state-run Rice Export Corporation of Pakistan (RECP) had started selling the new rice crop to exporters.
IRRI-6 export prices fell to $250 per tonne FOB in the week ended on Thursday from $270 on August 29, while basmati rates dropped to $490 from $500, Ghori said.
Basmati prices dropped after the RECP sold 10,000 tonnes at about $435 per tonne FOB by auction to an exporter and announced plans to sell another 10,000 tonnes next week.
"Prices fell sharply due to a lack of demand from abroad," Ghori said.
Exports fell 26.21 percent to 1.366 million worth $450 million in 1995/96 from 1.852 million worth $454 million in 1994/95.
